title: Incident-to-Eval Bridge and Auto-Smoke Generator for Config Deltas
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Multiple incidents in the last two quarters revealed gaps between incident signals and our eval coverage. Config or rollout changes (quantization profiles, KV cache TTLs, batching policy) have produced quality regressions that were not captured by existing smoke/eval suites. Purpose: Build an incident-driven pipeline that converts postmortems + incident traces into prioritized, runnable smoke tests and short eval harnesses that can be automatically added to pre-rollout checks and nightly regression sweeps. Key deliverables: 1) Incident-to-Eval Bridge service that ingests a postmortem artifact (trace/snapshot + config delta) and synthesizes a minimal prompt set + golden expectation. 2) Auto-Smoke Generator that produces executable smoke scripts (pytest style) and a CI job template. 3) Delta Prioritizer which scores candidate tests by estimated customer impact, reproduce-confidence, and resource cost. 4) Dashboard integration in Console to show newly generated tests, link back to incident and PR, and allow manual promotion to the canary suite. Acceptance criteria: - Postmortem -> smoke test flow works end-to-end for 3 historical incidents (KV-ttl drift, quantize-regression, and long-prefix batching mismatch) - Generated tests run in CI and fail on reproductions locally - New tests can be toggled into canary/weekly regression suites from Console UI - Run-time budget for auto tests per incident stays below 10 GPU-minutes on average Approach: Start with a lightweight transformer that extracts config deltas and request samples from incident artifacts. Use heuristics + small replay harness to find minimal seed prompts that reproduce the delta in scoring or logits. Wrap seeds into parameterized pytest units and attach context metadata (model variant, config snapshot, traffic sample). Build a small priority model (rules + weighted features) to rank tests. Integrate with existing eval infra (ENG-96318) for execution and with Console via a new endpoint. Risks: false positives (no actual regression), flakiness due to runtime nondeterminism, test explosion if we auto-generate every incident. Mitigations include manual triage gate for uncertain candidates, TTL/rotation for generated tests, and batching/quotas for CI runs.
